title: Bytewise cost & latency UX experiment notes
body:
Purpose and context:
This doc captures an exploratory set of wireframe ideas and lightweight experiment notes for a token/byte-level cost + latency breakdown view. Goal: give engineers and platform owners fast, actionable insight into which fragments of an invocation (by token position, by content span, by role) are driving unit cost and tail latency. This is a working doc — lots of rough sketches, assumptions, and open questions.

Problem statement (user pain):
- Customers tell us they can see overall per-invocation cost and p95 latency but can’t easily identify the precise spans of model execution that caused cost spikes (e.g., long system prompts vs assistant hallucinations).
- When multiple model variants and quantization profiles are in a rollout, teams need to know whether a cost jump is due to model change, sequence-length distribution, or cache miss patterns.
- Current token-level views are either too noisy or too aggregated; we need a medium that shows temporal structure without overwhelming detail.

Key design principles:
- Surface: a focused panel that surfaces the highest-signal slices first (heavy hitters).
- Correlate: show token-level heatmap + per-token latency + cache-hit indicators aligned with the text stream.
- Actionable: attach quick actions (open sample, link to invocation trace, pin as alert trigger, exclude from costing).
- Lightweight: default to sampled invocations with a one-click option to dive into full traces for retained sessions.

Proposed components (wireframe elements):
1) Stream overview rail (top)
   - Compact timeline summarizing request count, avg cost, avg latency per minute.
   - Tiny model badge row (shows model variant/quantization combo).

2) Invocation selector + heatmap canvas (left column)
   - Invocation list (sampled; shows short prompt, tokens, total cost, latency).
   - Heatmap: horizontal axis = token position; vertical axis = invocation. Color = normalized cost contribution (bytewise-weighted) with opacity for latency contribution.
   - Hover over cell shows: token string, token index, token-type (prompt/user/assistant), cost-by-µtokens, latency-ms, KV-cache-hit?

3) Token inspector (center detail pane)
   - Full text with inline colored underlines (cost intensity) and per-token micro-latency bars above tokens.
   - Compact legend with toggles: show cost | show latency | show cache-hits | show alignments to model-ops (attention, softmax hotspots).
   - Action buttons: open raw trace, create alert on token-slice, annotate and save as a flagged sample.

4) Waterfall by token-range (right column)
   - Aggregated bars for selected slice: queue time, kernel compute, memory copy, decoder loop, KV-lookup, post-processing. Percentage breakdown + absolute ms.
   - Suggested remediations based on patterns (heuristic suggestions): e.g., "High KV misses in middle-of-answer -> consider prefix caching for frequent prompts", "Long tail in post-processing -> evaluate JSON serializing with stream filtering".

Wireframe iterations (notes):
- v0 (sketch): pure heatmap + list. Too noisy when we show every invocation; reviewers wanted more aggregation controls.
- v1 (grouped): introduced clustering by prompt-template and short-summary rows. Reduced noise but hid outliers.
- v2 (hybrid): default aggregated view, with a toggle to expand to raw invocations. Added sampling controls and a pinned-sample track. This feels promising.

Behavioral notes and UX decisions to confirm:
- Sampling policy: default to 0.5% of invocations for the heatmap, ability to increase for a selected time window. Need product decision on retention/permission.
- Attribution weighting: use bytewise token length x model-cost-per-token for cost intensity; compute latency intensity as token-specific ms from microtraces. Edge case: subtokenization mapping needs to be visible.
- Privacy: flagged samples must respect PII redaction settings and team access controls.
- Alerting: allow a slice-level alert "Token slice cost exceeds X" that can trigger Slack + Runbook link.

Examples (mock scenarios to validate UX):
- Scenario A: sudden p95 increase after rollout -> view heatmap shows increased cost in leading system prompt tokens across many invocations; waterfall shows heavier kernel compute per token -> conclusion: model change caused more compute for same tokens.
- Scenario B: cost spikes only in a subset of invocations with long assistant responses -> token inspector shows long tail of generated tokens with many cache misses; remediation: tune cache policy / encourage prompt truncation.
- Scenario C: high cost on embed endpoints caused by long user-supplied contexts -> identify tokens near end of user context as hot spots. Suggest throttling or summarization.

Open questions / risks:
- Storage & performance: storing per-token microtraces at scale is heavy. Recommendation: store sampled microtraces + aggregates. Need SRE sizing estimate before committing. (SRE action: estimate additional storage for 1 month at 1% sampling)
- Visual scalability: how many invocations can the heatmap show before it becomes a blob? Proposed cap: 200 rows; beyond that auto-aggregate. Confirm with design experiments.
- Mapping model instrumentation: does every runtime provide token-level ms? We need clearly defined minimum trace contract from serving runtime. (ENG action: collect capabilities across Hosted/Dedicated/Private).

Notes from last session (2025-09-04 design workshop):
- Ravi: prefer latency waterfall pinned per slice, not per-invocation. Helps correlate kernel-level hotspots across many requests.
- Maya: add "role split" toggle to quickly compare system|user|assistant aggregate costs.
- Jonah: add a compact CSV export of selected slices so SRE/product can run offline stats.

Acceptance criteria for an initial MVP:
- Heatmap + invocation selector with hover details implemented.
- Token inspector with inline cost and latency overlays.
- Aggregated waterfall for a selected slice with suggested remediation text.
- Sampling control and export of flagged sample.

Next steps / TODOs:
- [ENG] Spike: instrument a small subset of model variants to emit token-level ms for 2 weeks (owner: Jonah). Due: 2025-09-19.
- [SRE] Estimate storage and query cost for 1% sampling for 90 days (owner: Camille). Due: 2025-09-12.
- [DESIGN] Produce Figma v2 with hybrid aggregated/expanded interaction and a compact mobile fallback (owner: Maya). Due: 2025-09-15.
- [PRODUCT] Decide default sampling rate and retention policy for console (owner: Ravi). Due: 2025-09-18.

Appendix: quick glossary and heuristics used in mockups:
- Bytewise-weighted cost: token_byte_length * model_unit_cost_per_token.
- Latency intensity: token_ms / total_invocation_ms.
- KV-cache-hit indicator: boolean from runtime trace; we show a small dot above token if miss.
- Slice: contiguous token range chosen by user or suggested by heavy-hitter algorithm.

Quick sketch references: Figma link in linked_artifacts. Please review and drop comments on the prototype. If you want to flag a sample for deeper investigation, right-click -> "Pin sample" in the prototype.

——
If you have additions, paste snippets of what you'd like to see in the token inspector (e.g., regex for system prompt markers, common stop-words to collapse).
